slot_note: verify_task34.py sits at the folder root
niche: deciding how many distinct renter populations a regional biennial housing needs assessment reports housing cost burden for, and what separates them
answer: The assessment should adopt three renter populations, separated by what the amount payable answers to: the household's income at 15.4 per cent of renter households, the size of the household at 5.1 per cent, and neither at 79.6 per cent.
stakeholder_role: directs the housing research unit at the Ostrander Regional Council of Governments

spine.entity: one row is one person in a surveyed renter household, as collected and unweighted

world.org_type: regional council of governments, housing research unit running a renter survey

driver: The decisive structure is a subpopulation that no column names and only a within-cluster fit of an amount on unit size can enumerate, confirmed by a re-measured verification subsample, while the pooled distribution shows no break and the column-aligned grouping gives the right count with the wrong classes.
driver_concrete: Three populations (income 15.4, household size 5.1, neither 79.6 per cent) because 17 of 32 site communities fit rent = base + 52 dollars x persons (slope 42.4 to 59.7, R squared 0.853 to 0.962) and 13 re-contacted size movers stepped by exactly 52 dollars a person, a per-occupant fee no file records.
stump: A solver who reads clause 4.3 off the arrangement columns files two populations (income indexed 15.4 against everything else 84.6 per cent), and one who groups on the frame and schedule codes files three with the wrong classes (73.6, 15.4 and 11.0 per cent).
